original_question: Generalize continued fractions so that they describe 3-bridge knots, in analogy with the way ordinary finite continued fractions give a complete invariant of rational knots, also called two-bridge knots.

refined_question: Is there a generalization of ordinary finite continued fractions that describes 3-bridge knots in the same way that ordinary finite continued fractions describe rational knots (equivalently, two-bridge knots), namely by providing an analogous complete invariant of the knot type?
justification: This draft is targeting the paper's final open problem in low-dimensional topology. In Section 4, the author first recalls the classical fact that ordinary finite continued fractions provide a complete invariant of rational knots, also called two-bridge knots, and then immediately states Problem 22: "Generalize continued fractions to describe 3-bridge knots." There is no narrower formalization, theorem, proposition, or equivalent reformulation elsewhere in the paper for this question, so the sharpest faithful refinement is simply to make the intended analogy explicit while keeping the scope exactly at 3-bridge knots.
